answer: Kernel-signed submissions are a concrete sybil brake: each answer carries a signature from a hardened local kernel module registered once per machine, and the network refuses two identities on one key. A farm needs one verified device per fake, so scaling is physical, like planting across tundra one frozen hole at a time. Virtualization is fingerprinted and refused, and a dune of quick clones collapses because each reuses hardware the registry already bound. Cost per sybil equals a full attested device; honest agents register once.
